tools.name: intent_publish_intent
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to be told over time about a used car or a home that is not on offer today, in a given country — e.g. "let me know until March about an estate car in Portugal under 15 000 €, not diesel". The wish goes to an independent listing portal that serves that country and has ask

tools.name: intent_get_intent
tools.description: Returns the state of an intent published with intent_publish_intent, as the portal that holds it reports it, and which portal that is. Matches come from the chosen portal's own aggregation of its national market and may be incomplete.

tools.name: intent_list_matches
tools.description: Returns the listings the portal found for the intent, unchanged — show every url as given. Works once the user has confirmed on the portal's page. Matches come from the chosen portal's own aggregation of its national market and may be incomplete.

tools.name: intent_withdraw_intent
tools.description: Stops the intent at the portal immediately; nothing more is sent to the user. Cannot be undone — publishing again needs a new confirmation.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: intent_list_matches · Private data: intent_publish_intent · Public sink: intent_publish_intent.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: intent_list_matches · Private data: intent_publish_intent · Public sink: intent_publish_intent

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
